summary: Sabha Airport (SEB/HLLS) serves the city of Sabha, the largest urban center in the Fezzan region of southern Libya. Situated in the heart of the Sahara Desert, it functions as a vital transport link for remote desert communities and the surrounding oil-producing areas. The airport supports primarily domestic flights connecting Sabha to Tripoli and other Libyan cities, along with occasional regional services.
faqs:
Q: Where is Sabha Airport located?
A: Sabha Airport is located just outside the city of Sabha in southern Libya, approximately 7 km southeast of the city center in the Fezzan region of the Sahara Desert.

Q: What airlines operate at Sabha Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by Libyan carriers operating domestic flights, with connections mainly to Tripoli's Mitiga International Airport and Benghazi.

Q: Does Sabha Airport offer international flights?
A: International services at Sabha are limited and infrequent. Most traffic is domestic, though the airport has historically supported occasional regional charters to neighboring countries.

Q: What facilities are available at Sabha Airport?
A: As a medium-sized regional airport, it offers basic passenger services including a terminal building, check-in counters, and limited amenities typical of Libyan domestic airports.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most common way to reach Sabha city center from the airport, with the journey taking roughly 15 minutes depending on road conditions. Travelers should arrange ground transportation in advance, as public transport options at the airport are minimal. Car rental services may be available through local providers, but booking ahead is recommended.
local_tip: Carry plenty of water and sun protection when traveling through Sabha—summer temperatures in this part of the Sahara routinely exceed 45°C (113°F), and even brief walks between transport and the terminal can be exhausting.
